messages:
incident-bot: URGENT: Observability alert triggered for inference-gateway: sustained increase in 5xx and downstream timeouts. batch-scheduler queue length spiked >5x across multiple shards starting 1869001200. severity=critical. paging oncall-sre.

alice (oncall-sre): I'm on it. paging @bob (runtime) and @carol (platform). Can someone confirm customer-facing impact? :rotating_light:

bob (runtime): looking now. seeing large backlog in batching-scheduler. per-shard backlog: shard-1=420, shard-2=380, shard-3=410. timeouts are concentrated at gateway->scheduler handoff.

carol (platform): grafana: https://grafana.redwood/graphs/ab12 queue depth and 95th latency jumped in same window. Noting a recent kernel rollout at 1859000000 that changed batching heuristics.

alice (oncall-sre): good catch. @deploy-bot did a canary kernel bump earlier?

deploy-bot: deploy: kernel-quant-v3 was promoted to canary at 1859999000, rolled to 40% of fleet. No automatic rollback triggered.

bob (runtime): command outputs:
```
$ curl -s http://scheduler-metrics.local/queue | jq .
{ "shard-1": {"queue_len": 420, "avg_wait_ms": 1200},
  "shard-2": {"queue_len": 380, "avg_wait_ms": 980},
  "shard-3": {"queue_len": 410, "avg_wait_ms": 1150} }
```

bob (runtime): seeing continuous batching windows blow up due to longer per-request decode times on canary kernels. KV cache hits dropped ~12% which amplifies token compute.

alice (oncall-sre): immediate mitigation ideas: 1) throttle gateway traffic to protect scheduler, 2) disable continuous-batching for high-latency model variants, 3) fallback route to smaller model variant for affected routes. Which is fastest?

dave (eng): fastest: add temporary 503 short-circuit from gateway for requests beyond concurrency threshold (protect downstream). I can push a routing rule within 5-7m.

carol (platform): I can flip continuous-batching off at runtime per-worker using feature flag: `FLAGS_CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=0` for canary pool. That should drain backlog eventually. Doing it for canary shards only first.

bob (runtime): doing health checks and draining plan. Steps:
1) mark canary nodes read-only to new long requests
2) set `batch_max_items=8` from 64 on canary
3) restart scheduler worker loop

bob (runtime): applying `batch_max_items=8` on shard-1 canary nodes now.

carol (platform): flipped flag on canary pool at 1869001260. Observability: queue_len on canary nodes starts to stabilize but cross-shard balancing still overloaded.

alice (oncall-sre): @erin (support) can you surface which customers reported errors? We need impact summary for execs.

erin (support): AcmeCorp reported timeouts, FinBeta saw 502s in logs, and some self-serve customers on hosted API saw elevated tail latency. Rough estimate: ~4-7% of requests experienced 5xx/timeouts in the last 25m. I'll pull precise numbers.

bob (runtime): additional mitigation: temporarily route high-latency models to smaller-quantized variant (v2-q4) that was stable. Doing traffic split 90/10 now for affected routes.

deploy-bot: traffic-split: model=large-rex -> fallback=large-rex-q4 split=90/10 applied at 1869001280.

alice (oncall-sre): big picture: we suspect kernel-quant-v3 increases per-token decode CPU/GPU time causing batching backlog -> HOL-like blocking when large requests sit at head of batch queue causing tail timeouts.

bob (runtime): confirmed. stack traces show long tail on `runtime_decode` and more time spent in kernel launch.

carol (platform): immediate customer-facing mitigations done: throttling rule + batch_max_items reduction + traffic split to q4. Observed 95th latency drop from 1.2s to 340ms on stabilized nodes over 5m.

alice (oncall-sre): update PD: paging closed for urgent wake-up, we are actively remediating. Assigning postmortem and owner. @dave will lead postmortem.

dave (eng): I'll own postmortem. timeline + RCA + corrective actions. Will create postmortem doc and include follow-ups: rollback canary to previous kernel, add canary safety circuit to auto-roll back on queue depth anomaly, and add per-shard batch-depth throttles.

erin (support): compiling customer impact notes: will notify top impacted accounts and set status page draft.

alice (oncall-sre): action items (short):
- bob: verify full drain and monitor error rate until <0.5% (ETA 20m)
- carol: coordinate rollback of kernel canary or limit canary pool to 0% if instability continues
- dave: create postmortem and mitigation plan (ETA 24h)
- erin: customer comms + status page update (ETA 15m)

bob (runtime): queue metrics: now shard-1=85, shard-2=70, shard-3=92 as of 1869001330. Error rate down to 1.6%. continuing watch.

carol (platform): rolling kernel canary back to 0% in 5m window if error rate doesn't continue to fall.

alice (oncall-sre): great. leave this thread open for handoff. I'll be on until error rate <0.5% then sign off. If anyone adds anything after handoff, prefix with `handoff:`

sre-bot: NOTE: created incident page https://incidents.redwood/1869001234 and assigned incident-id: INC-2026-042.

alice (oncall-sre): handoff to night oncall at 1869001345: @dave will take primary while I stand down. dave, please monitor for 2h and escalate if anything regresses.

dave (eng): ack. monitoring dashboards, alert thresholds tightened. Will update thread with any regressions.

erin (support): sent initial customer emails and status page published as draft.

alice (oncall-sre): signing off. Good mitigation work. We'll follow up with RCA + durable fixes. :white_check_mark:
